{"decision":"RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Nothing here is chosen.

ANTHONY, 2026-09-22, in his own words: "I was thinking of creating a dev_reflow repo that is over both flo2 and reflow2, but the difference here between all the other examples is that both reflow2 and flo2 are already reflow2 designs." And the cost that prompted it: "I'm getting tired of relaying info between the two sessions or asking one session agent about a topic that is about how reflow2 and flo2 will work together."

⭐ WHAT THE SEARCH FOUND FIRST, so nobody re-derives it. Five nodes already hold parts of this and each answers a DIFFERENT question:
  · `dec:nested-graphs` (ACCEPTED) — a graph per OWNERSHIP boundary, levels inside each. "THE HIERARCHY DOES NOT DECIDE; AUTHORITY DOES." One owner here, so the rule sends reflow2 and flo2 to separate graphs only because they RELEASE separately.
  · `dec:idea-one-owner-many-projects` (open) — where the boundary goes when one person works many interrelated projects. His case, at the level of placement.
  · `dec:idea-a-session-holds-several-graphs` (open) — which graphs a SESSION can see; already names reflow2 + flo2 by name, already holds the union framing, the mutable/immutable framing, and a trial.
  · `dec:idea-a-top-level-graph-holds-what-the-component-graphs-share` (DEFERRED, shape only) — Alex's system-of-systems ask, narrowed to "a graph per tier linked vertically". Closest in SHAPE and different in SUBJECT: Alex's children are tiers of one product; these children are two products.
  · `dec:idea-intent-crosses-designs` — whether a mirrored Decision is BINDING on the far side or only VISIBLE.

⭐⭐ WHAT IS GENUINELY NEW, and it is not the hierarchy:

1. **THE CHILDREN ARE PRODUCTS, NOT PARTS.** Every existing framing has the parent DECOMPOSING into the children — intent down, evidence up, with arithmetic attached. reflow2 and flo2 are not parts of dev_reflow. Neither realizes it. A parent that cannot decompose has no roll-up to perform, so the whole vertical apparatus the tier node argues about does not apply, and what the parent is FOR has to be answered from scratch.

2. **THE MOTIVATING OBJECT IS A DECISION THAT BELONGS TO THE PAIR.** "a topic that is about how reflow2 and flo2 will work together" is not a decision in reflow2's design, nor one in flo2's. It is about the relation. Today it has no home, so it lives in whichever session happened to raise it, and the other session never learns it. That is a sharper statement of the need than "I want a top-level graph", and it may have a cheaper answer.

3. **THE PARENT'S SUBJECT INCLUDES THE TOOL.** dev_reflow would be a reflow2 design whose subject matter is partly reflow2 itself. That is not fatal — this repo already is one — but it puts the parent squarely in the path of the standing rule that reflow2 is a wrench and never a thing built for itself.

🛑 MEASURED TODAY, 2026-09-22, BEFORE WEIGHING ANY OPTION — and it reframes the ask:
  · **ZERO nodes in reflow2's design carry `mirror_of`.** Identical to the reading taken 2026-08-12. The mirroring layer is still built, still shipped, still never kept on a real pair.
  · **reflow2's graph holds NO flo2 Project, Component or Interface at all.** Nothing here knows flo2 exists structurally.
  ⇒ So whatever link flo2 holds, it is one-directional at best, and the reflow2 side of it is empty. "flo2 doesn't always remember it has access" may not be a memory problem — there may be nothing standing to remember. THAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: flo2's graph was not read, and only a reading there can tell an absent link from a forgotten one.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN.

(a) A THIRD GRAPH HOLDING ONLY WHAT BELONGS TO THE PAIR — cross-design decisions, the seam, shared vocabulary; the children stay independent and neither is decomposed. Cheap in that it needs no new vocabulary: a graph is a graph. Counter: it is a third place to forget, and the forgetting is the stated problem. It also inherits the refresh defect below.

(b) THE PAIR'S DECISIONS LIVE IN THE UPSTREAM (reflow2). flo2 depends on reflow2, so reflow2's design is the one both sessions have reason to read, and this repo's export is already committed and checked in CI. Counter: it puts flo2's product decisions in a design that is meant to be a general-purpose tool, which is the self-absorption the wrench rule names.

(c) THE PAIR'S DECISIONS LIVE IN THE CONSUMER (flo2). The relation matters to flo2 more than to reflow2, and flo2 is where the consequences land. Counter: reflow2 then cannot see what is being decided about it, which is the direction that already fails — see the measurement above.

(d) NO NEW GRAPH; THE SESSION HOLDS BOTH. Already argued at length under `dec:idea-a-session-holds-several-graphs`, with a trial. Counter, MEASURED in that node: `mirror_surface` has no refresh — a second mirror of the same design collides with itself, leaves the stale node in place, and leaves `mirrors` reporting the old pin, so the staleness register READS FRESH after a failed refresh. A federation of independently-moving projects is made of refreshes. That blocker sits under (a), (d) and any mirroring answer.

(e) ⭐ FIX THE FORGETTING, NOT THE TOPOLOGY. If the measured cost is relaying between sessions, and the cause is that nothing in flo2's orientation names the link it already has, then the repair is at the orientation step and no new graph is needed. Supporting evidence from this design: `upstream_status` exists, and `fact:the-upstream-moved-nag-withholds-the-path-it-is-already-carrying` (flo2 F17) records that the one loop_status line telling an agent to go and read the upstream is the only one that names no tool, no file and no path. And the nag fires only when the upstream MOVED — so on a quiet day nothing mentions the link at all. Counter: this answers the friction and not the question. A decision that belongs to the pair still has no home, whoever remembers to look.

WHAT WOULD DECIDE IT, and it is one reading in flo2's graph: does flo2 hold mirrored reflow2 nodes, or a declared external dependency, or neither? Neither ⇒ (e) is not even available yet and the first move is to make the link exist. A declared dependency that nothing surfaces ⇒ (e) is the cheap answer. A kept, refreshed mirror that still gets forgotten ⇒ the topology options earn their cost.

SHARPENED 2026-09-22 — THE HUB BECOMES A TIERED ORGANISATION WITH AUTHORITY FLOWING DOWN
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, the same day, extending his own idea.

HIS WORDS: "having the dev_reflow project that is more of a design hub over both projects. This allows me to focus on any aspect of flo2 or reflow2 without having to jump between two different sessions. Secondly, in having a management/master_design project, what if both sub-projects offered up their designs to be held in a master design project… the master project could consider all aspects of the designs within it and secondly, has both full read/write authority over both projects. From an organization level, maybe project A and project B are under group K and project C and project D are under group J and both group K and group J are under division Q. You could have a responsible user at each tier that manages the projects below it. Even project A through project D have a responsible designer responsible for that component of the design. This kind of matches with a hierarchy of systems engineering. Tier 0 may be systems-of-systems level which is equivalent to the division Q… The systems level could be equivalent to the group J and K and the sub-systems/components could be project A through D."

⭐⭐ THE UNLOCK, AND IT REVERSES THIS NODE'S OPENING PREMISE. The original entry above says the children are PRODUCTS rather than PARTS, so the parent has no roll-up to perform and must justify itself from scratch. THAT WAS TRUE OF A TWO-PRODUCT PAIR AND IS NOT TRUE OF THIS. An org ladder — division over groups over projects — is a decomposition again, and the thing decomposed is AUTHORITY rather than assembly.

AND THAT MAKES IT CONSISTENT WITH THE ACCEPTED RULE RATHER THAN A STRAIN ON IT. `dec:nested-graphs` (ACCEPTED 2026-07-25): "A design is its own graph when something at that level is separately OWNED, separately RELEASED, or separately SHARED — and a subtree of one graph otherwise. THE HIERARCHY DOES NOT DECIDE; AUTHORITY DOES." Anthony's tiers each carry A RESPONSIBLE PERSON. So every tier IS an ownership boundary by the rule's own test, and a graph per tier is what the rule prescribes — not an exception to it. `dec:idea-one-owner-many-projects` records that his case sat on a seam in that rule because he had one owner and many release trains; a tiered organisation with a responsible person per tier does not sit on that seam at all.

⭐ THE AUTHORITY DIRECTION IS THE GENUINELY NEW CLAIM, and it has a home that already argues the opposite case for a DIFFERENT relation. `dec:idea-gap-flows-to-the-dependency` asks how a downstream owner levies a requirement on an upstream design THEY DO NOT OWN, and Anthony's own lean there is (A) WRITE-ONLY-AT-PROPOSED — file it like an issue, the maintainer triages. Its framing: "a CUSTOMER REQUIREMENT LEVIED ON A SUPPLIER, the most ordinary transaction in the discipline."

⇒ THESE DO NOT CONFLICT; THEY PARTITION. Across an ownership boundary, write-only-at-proposed. WITHIN one — a tier owner and the tiers beneath them — full read/write is not a violation at all, because the authority is already theirs. The question each asks is the same question at opposite sides of one line, and the line is the thing `dec:nested-graphs` already named.

⭐ "OFFERED UP" IS THE PART THAT MAKES IT SAFE, AND IT IS A REAL DISTINCTION. His phrasing is that the sub-projects OFFER their designs up, not that the master reaches down and takes them. That makes the master's reach GRANTED by the child rather than ASSERTED by the parent — which is how a real organisation works, is expressible today (`export_surface` + `designation`), and leaves a child able to withhold. A parent that simply helps itself to its children's stores is a different and much stronger claim, and nobody has asked for it.

🛑 AND TODAY MEASURED WHAT "OFFERING UP" COSTS WHEN NOBODY DOES IT. 2026-09-22: reflow2 held 262 Requirements with ZERO marked `published`, so flo2 — which had mirrored it correctly — received 22 nodes of pure structure and not one Requirement, Capability or Decision. The offering mechanism was built, verified, documented and used by nobody, and every signal read green. A tier model rests entirely on children offering something worth holding; this is the measurement of what happens when they do not, and it is why `published_surface_carries_no_intent` now exists.

🎯 THE DEFERRAL NEXT DOOR HAS JUST HAD ITS RE-ASK TRIGGER FIRED, AND NOBODY SHOULD HAVE TO NOTICE THAT BY ACCIDENT. `dec:idea-a-top-level-graph-holds-what-the-component-graphs-share` is DEFERRED, SHAPE ONLY, behind `req:decomposition-covers-its-parent`, and names its own re-ask conditions: "(i) a real design is split across an authority boundary and someone needs a parent's number to mean something, (ii) `dec:idea-intent-crosses-designs` is settled, or (iii) A SECOND USER ASKS FOR TIERS." Alex asked first, on 2026-08-14. Anthony has now asked, in the same shape, for the same thing. ⇒ (iii) IS MET. That node's option (b) — a graph per tier, linked vertically — is the stated starting position, and the deferral was about SEQUENCING, never about the shape being wrong.

🛑 THE MODELLING TRAP THAT NODE NAMED, AND IT BITES HARDER HERE BECAUSE HIS LADDER IS EXPLICITLY ORGANISATIONAL. `Component.level` (component → subsystem → system → system_of_systems → enterprise) is an ASSEMBLY ladder: *part of*. Division/group/project is an AUTHORITY ladder: *answerable to*. They look identical written down and they are different relations — a project is not a PART of a division, it REPORTS to one. His own mapping ("tier 0 may be systems-of-systems… equivalent to division Q") puts the two ladders side by side, which is exactly where conflating them becomes easy. `hierarchy_issues` already reads `level` the assembly way, so reusing it would give wrong answers silently.

📌 WHAT IS ALREADY BUILT TOWARD THE READING HALF, so the gap is narrower than it sounds: `req:analyse-at-any-level` is ACCEPTED and `cap:scoped-analysis` delivers it — "a team asks the detectors about its own part, and is told what it did not see". A tier owner asking about their own tier is that call. What does NOT exist is anything that ROLLS UP across a design boundary: `dec:idea-a-top-level-graph-holds-what-the-component-graphs-share` measured it — reads are scoped to the bound `graph_id` and `create_edge` resolves both endpoints in scope, so a DECOMPOSES edge between two graphs cannot be created at all, and `export_surface` carries no Verifications, so the EVIDENCE is exactly the part that does not cross.

📌 AND THE PER-NODE PRIMITIVE HIS "RESPONSIBLE DESIGNER" NEEDS ALREADY HAS A REQUIREMENT: `req:a-node-can-say-who-may-change-it` — "A node can declare who may change it, so 'what may I change alone?' is answerable from the graph rather than from prose." A tier model with a responsible person per level is that requirement at organisational scale.

NEW OPTIONS THIS FRAMING ADDS, NONE CHOSEN.

(f) A GRAPH PER TIER, N DEEP, each with a responsible Contributor, authority flowing down and evidence rolling up. What Alex asked for and what Anthony has now asked for independently. Cost, and it is the honest one: nothing rolls up across a graph boundary today, so the parent's numbers mean nothing until that is built — which is precisely the sequencing the other node deferred behind.

(g) ONE GRAPH, TIERS AS LEVELS INSIDE IT, with the responsible person recorded per subtree. Needs no cross-graph anything, and `cap:scoped-analysis` already reads it. Counter: gives up separate write locks, separate release trains, and the ability to share one project without shipping the others — which is most of what a tier split is for, and Anthony's projects DO release separately.

(h) THE HUB HOLDS ONLY WHAT SPANS ITS CHILDREN — cross-project intent and the seams — and never mirrors their internals. Smallest version of (f); the parent is a peer with a wider view rather than an authority. Counter: it does not answer the session-jumping complaint, which is about seeing EVERYTHING from one place.

⚠️ WHAT NOBODY HAS ANSWERED, AND IT IS THE SAME HOLE IN EVERY OPTION: `rule:design-intent-moves-only-on-the-owners-word` is ENFORCED and CHECKED IN CI. If division Q's responsible user accepts a requirement inside project A, WHOSE WORD IS THAT? Either the rule means the tier owner (and "owner" becomes a ladder rather than a name), or it means project A's designer (and the tier owner's write authority stops short of settling intent). Both are defensible, they give different products, and `check_intent_authority.py` would need to know which. Nothing in the design says.

RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING AND AS A LEAN, NOT AS A SETTLEMENT — he said "my first reaction is".

HIS WORDS: "if I was the chief designer over reflow2 and flo2… when I made a decision, should it stay in the reflow2 or flo2 graphs or should it be put in the dev_reflow2 level project graph? My first reaction is that it should stay in the lowest level. For example if I discovered that flo2 required something from reflow2, the dev_reflow2 should put this requirement in the reflow2 graph and not the dev_reflow2 graph. This makes the dev_reflow2 level more of a read its sub design graphs and then has the authority to update those graphs. It doesn't really have its own graph in other words other than maybe a minimal one… but the design still lives in those sub-graphs."

And the reason, from the A-staff form: "if the general had his own requirements in his/her design graph as well as there were requirements in the A5's design graph, then you lose a single source of truth and it can lead to conflicts between contrary requirements."

⭐⭐ THIS IS A DIFFERENT ARCHITECTURE FROM EVERY OPTION ABOVE, AND IT DISSOLVES THREE BLOCKERS RATHER THAN SOLVING THEM.

1. **THE CROSS-GRAPH EDGE IS NOT NEEDED FOR y.** Options (a), (f) and (g) all assumed the parent holds design that must relate to the children's — so `DECOMPOSES` had to cross a boundary, which `create_edge` refuses because it resolves both endpoints in scope. **A hub holding no design has nothing to relate.** The blocker recorded above as shared between x and y turns out to bind x only.

2. **THE MIRROR REFRESH DEFECT IS NOT ON THIS PATH EITHER.** A hub that READS its children's live graphs holds no pinned copy, so there is nothing to refresh and nothing to go stale. The refresh defect still blocks the x-axis and every peer-to-peer mirroring answer; it does not block this.

3. **IT ANSWERS THE "WHOSE WORD IS IT" HOLE THIS NODE RAISED, WITH EXISTING VOCABULARY.** The question was: if a tier owner settles a requirement inside a child, whose word is that? Under this model the requirement LIVES in the child and carries `AUTHORED_BY role=approver` naming the tier owner. `rule:design-intent-moves-only-on-the-owners-word` and `check_intent_authority.py` work UNCHANGED — the rule asks whether a settled node carries a name, never which building the name sits in. No new authority model is needed.

⭐ AND THE ARGUMENT FOR IT IS THE STRONGEST ONE ANYWHERE IN THIS THREAD, because it is about correctness rather than convenience: TWO PLACES TO WRITE A REQUIREMENT IS TWO SOURCES OF TRUTH, and the failure is not that the parent's copy goes stale — it is that the parent's copy can CONTRADICT the child's and nothing is wrong in either graph. A design that permits that has no single source of truth by construction.

⚠️ WHAT IT DOES NOT SOLVE, AND IT IS THE THING THAT STARTED THIS NODE. The stated cost was session-jumping: "I'm getting tired of relaying info between the two sessions." A hub that reads its children needs to READ TWO GRAPHS AT ONCE, and today a session is bound to exactly one. So the hub's value on day one is the ROSTER and the AUTHORITY RECORD, not the reading — and the session-jumping stays until multi-graph access exists (`dec:idea-a-session-holds-several-graphs`). That node stops being one option among several and becomes THE dependency.

📌 AND THE APPARENT CONFLICT WITH AN ACCEPTED REQUIREMENT IS ALREADY RESOLVED IN THIS DESIGN — it is just not written as a decision. `req:a-session-cannot-reach-another-designs-graph` is accepted, is a stated SECURITY property, and was published to consumers on 2026-09-22. It reads as forbidding exactly what a hub needs. `dec:idea-a-session-holds-several-graphs` already draws the line: "MULTI-TENANT ISOLATION (strangers' projects on a hosted server, must not see each other) is not the same as COMPOSITION (one author's own interdependent designs, useless apart)… but nothing in the design says so yet." ⇒ The distinction exists in prose on an open idea and nowhere as a settled position, so a reader meeting the accepted requirement alone would conclude the hub is forbidden. That is worth settling BEFORE anything is built, and it is cheap to settle.

📌 WHAT THE "MINIMAL GRAPH" WOULD HOLD, since he anticipates one: the roster of children, the authority record (who may write into which), and the honest residual — a decision that belongs to the RELATION rather than to either side. His own example routes cleanly (flo2 needs something from reflow2 ⇒ the requirement goes in reflow2's graph), but a genuine seam decision — "flo2 talks to reflow2 over MCP, not REST" — has two sides, and which child owns it is not obvious. Under single-source-of-truth the answer is probably that the CONTRACT lives as an Interface on both sides and the DECISION lives wherever it constrains; that is a guess and nobody has tested it.

🎯 THE TRIAL THIS SUGGESTS, and it is small: stand dev_reflow2 up with a minimal graph holding only the roster and the authority record, work from it for a week, and measure whether the session-jumping actually falls.
